newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy industry says key pension reform or no talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy industry says key pension reform or no talks.

text.p: Italy's employers' body Confindustria will not sit down with government and unions to discuss streamlining the welfare state unless partial reforms made to the unwieldy pension system two years ago are also on the agenda, Confindustria chairman Giorgio Fossa said.

Fossa, speaking to reporters at a chemical industry meeting, said he was unhappy about comments by UIL union leader Pietro Larizza earlier today who indicated he was against any of the 1995 reforms being altered.

The changes implemented when current Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini headed a technocrat government introduced a graduated increase in the pensionable age and the opening up of a pay-as-you-go contributions system.
"Larizza's comments worry me," said Fossa. "On these conditions we will not sit down at the same table."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government is due to start negotiations with unions and employers on reforming the welfare state on June 18.

"Reform must affect in a structural way all parts of the welfare state otherwise it would be condemned to self-distruction," Fossa said, adding that length of service pensions must be abolished. Under this system, many Italians can draw a pension years before reaching pensionable age.

Confindustria was prepared for the negotiations starting on June 18 and going on for as long as necessary, even without a summer break, until an accord was reached on restoring to the welfare state "the role for which it was created -- helping those in need and not everyone indiscriminately," Fossa said.
